zh.principle: **标准**：网络安全供应链风险管理实践（SP 800-161）（Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices for Systems and Organizations (SP 800-161 Rev.摘要写明它的性质：「This publication provides guidance to organizations on identifying, assessing, and mitigating cybersecurity risks throughout the supply chain at all levels of their organizations.」做法是嵌进已有的风险管理：「The publication integrates cybersecurity supply chain risk management (C-SCRM) into risk management activities by applying a multilevel, C-SCRM-specific approach」。§1.1 为 C-SCRM 下定义：「Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) is a systematic process for managing exposure to cybersecurity risks throughout the supply chain and developing appropriate response strategies, policies, processes, and procedures.」三段依次给出文件性质、实施路径与术语定义：它是给组织的指导，做法是把 C-SCRM 嵌入既有风险管理并分层实施，定义把管理对象说成暴露面连同响应策略、政策、过程与程序。
zh.why: 起点是买方的不可见性。摘要首句：「Organizations are concerned about the risks associated with products and services that may potentially contain malicious functionality, are counterfeit, or are vulnerable due to poor manufacturing and development practices within the supply chain.」并把根源归到过程看不见：「These risks are associated with an enterprise's decreased visibility into and understanding of how the technology they acquire is developed, integrated, and deployed」。§1 因此先定义对象：「In this document, the term supply chain refers to the linked set of resources and processes between and among multiple levels of an enterprise, each of which is an acquirer that begins with the sourcing of products and services and extends through the product and service life cycle.」引文把风险分成两层：产品或服务本身可能含恶意功能、是假冒的、或因制造与开发过程不佳而脆弱；买方看不见技术如何被开发、集成与部署。§1 的定义补充说链条上的每一层自身也是买方。
zh.used: §2 给出接入点：「C-SCRM should be integrated into the enterprise-wide risk management process described in [SP80039] and depicted in Fig.3.」责任由组织共同承担：「Implementing C-SCRM requires enterprises to establish a coordinated team-based approach and a shared responsibility model to effectively manage cybersecurity risks throughout the supply chain.」并就跨部门输入给出建议（原文 should aim to，不是要求）：「Enterprises should aim to infuse perspectives from multiple disciplines and processes」。§1.4 为不同读者指路，对企业风险管理的读者写：「The entire document is relevant to and recommended for readers fitting this profile.」三句的主语都是企业自身：接入既有的风险管理过程、建立协同团队与共担责任模型、把多学科的视角注入做法；§1.4 的分读只是指引。
zh.broken: 文件自陈两处不做。§1 划出与一般供应链风险管理的分界：「This publication does not address many of the non-cybersecurity aspects of SCRM.」§1.1 说明它不给路线图：「However, this publication does not offer a specific roadmap for enterprises to follow to reach various states of capability and maturity.」并强调须裁剪：「The C-SCRM guidance provided in this document is not one-size-fits-all.」前两句是主题上的分界，第三句是方法上的告诫：实践须按各企业的规模、资源与风险情形裁剪。另有一处限制属于这份副本：页眉写「May 2022 INCLUDES UPDATES AS OF 11-01-2024; SEE APPENDIX K」，而留存文本止于 §2.3.1 的责任表，第 3 章的关键实践与页眉所指的附录 K 都不在这份文本里，其内容在此不作断言。
zh.history: 页眉首行为「NIST Special Publication 800 NIST SP 800-161r1-upd1」，日期行写明「May 2022 INCLUDES UPDATES AS OF 11-01-2024; SEE APPENDIX K」，DOI 行是「This publication is available free of charge from:」，DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-161r1-upd1。出版史块记录评审与取代关系：「Approved by the NIST Editorial Review Board on 2024-09-25 Supersedes NIST Special Publication 800-161r1 (May 2022)」，引用行给六位作者与年份并补一句「Includes updates as of November 1, 2024.」——「Boyens J, Smith A, Bartol N, Winkler K, Holbrook A, Fallon M (2022) Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices for Systems and Organizations.」致谢页另记 2015 年版作者：「the original authors of NIST SP 800-161, Celia Paulsen (NIST), Rama Moorthy (Hatha Systems), and Stephanie Shankles」。以上引文都出自这份留存文本自己的门面板块，合起来给出时间线：2022 年 5 月的第一修订、2024 年 11 月 1 日并入的更新、2024 年 9 月 25 日的评审批准，以及被取代的 800-161r1。

en.principle: **Standard**: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices for Systems and Organizations (SP 800-161 Rev. 1) (网络安全供应链风险管理实践（SP 800-161）). The abstract gives its character: "This publication provides guidance to organizations on identifying, assessing, and mitigating cybersecurity risks throughout the supply chain at all levels of their organizations." The method is integration into existing risk management: "The publication integrates cybersecurity supply chain risk management (C-SCRM) into risk management activities by applying a multilevel, C-SCRM-specific approach". Section 1.1 defines the term: "Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) is a systematic process for managing exposure to cybersecurity risks throughout the supply chain and developing appropriate response strategies, policies, processes, and procedures." In order the three quotations give the character of the document, its method and its definition: guidance for organizations, delivered by embedding C-SCRM in existing risk management and working it through the levels, with the managed object stated as exposure together with response strategies, policies, processes and procedures.
en.why: The starting point is the acquirer's lack of visibility. The abstract opens: "Organizations are concerned about the risks associated with products and services that may potentially contain malicious functionality, are counterfeit, or are vulnerable due to poor manufacturing and development practices within the supply chain." and attributes it to unseen processes: "These risks are associated with an enterprise's decreased visibility into and understanding of how the technology they acquire is developed, integrated, and deployed". Section 1 therefore defines the object first: "In this document, the term supply chain refers to the linked set of resources and processes between and among multiple levels of an enterprise, each of which is an acquirer that begins with the sourcing of products and services and extends through the product and service life cycle." The quotations separate two layers: products and services may carry malicious functionality, be counterfeit, or be weakly built, and the acquirer cannot see how the technology is developed, integrated and deployed. The §1 definition adds that every level of the chain is itself an acquirer.
en.used: Section 2 gives the point of attachment: "C-SCRM should be integrated into the enterprise-wide risk management process described in [SP80039] and depicted in Fig. 3." The duty is shared organisationally: "Implementing C-SCRM requires enterprises to establish a coordinated team-based approach and a shared responsibility model to effectively manage cybersecurity risks throughout the supply chain." and cross-functional input is advised in should-aim-to terms: "Enterprises should aim to infuse perspectives from multiple disciplines and processes". Section 1.4 routes readers, telling enterprise risk owners: "The entire document is relevant to and recommended for readers fitting this profile." The subject of all three sentences is the enterprise itself: attach C-SCRM to the existing risk management process, build a coordinated team with a shared responsibility model, and infuse perspectives from several disciplines; the §1.4 reading routes are guidance.
en.broken: Two exclusions are its own. Section 1 separates C-SCRM from the wider discipline: "This publication does not address many of the non-cybersecurity aspects of SCRM." Section 1.1 declines to give a roadmap: "However, this publication does not offer a specific roadmap for enterprises to follow to reach various states of capability and maturity." and warns against copying it verbatim: "The C-SCRM guidance provided in this document is not one-size-fits-all." The first two mark a subject boundary and the third a method warning: the practices must be tailored to the size, resources and risk situation of each enterprise. A separate limit belongs to this retained copy: the masthead reads "May 2022 INCLUDES UPDATES AS OF 11-01-2024; SEE APPENDIX K", while the text held here stops at the responsibility table in section 2.3.1, so the key practices of Section 3 and the Appendix K named there are outside this file and their contents are not asserted.
en.history: The first masthead line reads "NIST Special Publication 800 NIST SP 800-161r1-upd1", the date line reads "May 2022 INCLUDES UPDATES AS OF 11-01-2024; SEE APPENDIX K", and the DOI line reads "This publication is available free of charge from:" followed by the DOI 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-161r1-upd1. The publication history block records the review and the supersession: "Approved by the NIST Editorial Review Board on 2024-09-25 Supersedes NIST Special Publication 800-161r1 (May 2022)", and the citation line gives the six authors, the year and the note "Includes updates as of November 1, 2024." followed by "Boyens J, Smith A, Bartol N, Winkler K, Holbrook A, Fallon M (2022) Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Practices for Systems and Organizations." The acknowledgements also name the 2015 edition's authors: "the original authors of NIST SP 800-161, Celia Paulsen (NIST), Rama Moorthy (Hatha Systems), and Stephanie Shankles". All of these quotations come from the front matter of the retained text and give one timeline: the May 2022 first revision, the updates incorporated as of 1 November 2024, the editorial approval of 25 September 2024, and the superseded SP 800-161r1.

zh: C-SCRM：网络安全供应链风险管理，本文件的主题。
supply chain：多层买方之间从采购延伸到产品与服务生命周期的资源与过程集合。
acquirer：供应链上的采购方，本文件把每一层都视为 acquirer。
multilevel risk management：企业、任务与业务流程、运行三个层次的风险管理。
FASC：联邦采购安全委员会，由 2018 年的 FASCSA 设立。
Foundational / Sustaining / Enabling：本文件对 C-SCRM 实践给出的粗略优先级。
en: C-SCRM: cybersecurity supply chain risk management, the subject of this file.
Supply chain: the linked resources and processes across enterprise levels, from sourcing through the life cycle.
Acquirer: the buying party; this publication treats every level of the chain as one.
Multilevel risk management: risk management at the enterprise, mission and business process, and operational levels.
FASC: the Federal Acquisition Security Council created by the 2018 FASCSA.
Foundational / Sustaining / Enabling: the rough prioritisation of C-SCRM practices given here.
